history.dynasty: none (modern, built by a charitable trust)
history.summary: Modern Hindu temple complex on a hill near Bundu (Edalhatu), about 40 km southeast of Ranchi on the Ranchi-Tata highway (NH-43). Built by Sanskriti Vihar, a charitable trust headed by Shri Sita Ram Maroo of the Ranchi Express Group; foundation stone laid by Swami Vasudevanand Saraswati on 24 October 1991 and prana pratishtha performed by Swami Vamdev Ji Maharaj on 10 July 1994. Designed as a giant chariot with 18 carved wheels and seven horses in imitation of the mythical chariot of Surya and inspired by Konark; includes a pond for Chhath rituals, subsidiary shrines (Shiva, Parvati, Ganesha), and a dharamshala. (verify) The brief's '51-ft' height figure appears in no consulted source and is left out; one directory mentions a 2.5-foot Surya idol, which is likewise unverified. CSV town 'Ranchi' corrected to actual locality Bundu (Ranchi district).

name: Sun Temple
town_description: Bundu is a town in Ranchi district, Jharkhand, on the Ranchi-Tata highway (NH-43), about 40 km southeast of Ranchi. The temple stands on a hill beside the highway at Edalhatu.

travel.road: Directly on the Ranchi-Tata highway (NH-43) near Bundu; all-weather motorable road to the temple premises

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Chhath Puja (October-November) is the peak festival
visitor_information.opening_hours: Daylight hours; special arrangements during Chhath Puja (verify locally)
